parameters.name: region
parameters.description:
**Which storefront to read.** Optional; default `ae`.

- `ae`  -  United Arab Emirates, prices in AED.
- `sa`  -  Saudi Arabia, prices in SAR.
- `eg`  -  Egypt, prices in EGP.
- `kw`  -  Kuwait, prices in KWD.
- `qa`  -  Qatar, prices in QAR.
- `om`  -  Oman, prices in OMR.
- `bh`  -  Bahrain, prices in BHD.

`ae`, `sa` and `eg` are separate catalogues: the same product can have a different price, different sellers, or not exist at all. `kw`, `qa`, `om` and `bh` sell the `ae` assortment in their own currency, at their own prices and with their own delivery estimates. `/marketplace` reports which catalogue serves a storefront, on `serving_catalogue`.

The pickup network (`/collection-points`) exists only on `ae`, `sa` and `eg`.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description:
**Which branch of the tree to return.** Optional.

- **Omitted**  -  the **16 top-level departments**, each with its immediate children. This is the seed for a traversal.
- `fashion`  -  that department in full.
- `fashion/women-31229/shoes-16238`  -  that branch.
- `shoes-16238`  -  the same branch. Resolution is by the **last segment**, so the short form and the full path are interchangeable.

**A path is answered with the whole chain from its root down.** Asking for a deep leaf returns its root department with the requested branch nested inside; read downward to the node whose `path` you asked for.

Paths come from this endpoint (call it without `category`, then follow any node's `path`) and from the `breadcrumbs` on any listing or product response. `/category-products` takes any of them.

A path that resolves to nothing is a **404 naming what it matched instead**, never a confident 200 over the wrong branch.

url.description:
**A noon search, category, brand or seller page URL.** Required.

- `https://www.noon.com/uae-en/fashion/women-31229/shoes-16238`  -  a category.
- `https://www.noon.com/uae-en/apple`  -  a brand.
- `https://www.noon.com/uae-en/p-75886`  -  a seller storefront.

The last three look alike; the response says which one the URL named, on `resolved_as`. Every filter and paging parameter on this endpoint applies on top of it.

page.description:

**A single query returns at most 10,000 products**  -  50 pages of 200. Values above 50 are a 400. Page on `pagination.has_more`; a page past the last one comes back empty.

page_size.description:
**How many products per page.** Optional; default `50`, maximum `200`.

**A single query returns at most 10,000 products**  -  50 pages of 200. The limit is per query: split a larger result set (a narrower category, a price window, one brand at a time) and each narrower query gets its own window. `totals.exceeds_retrievable_cap` on the response says when a split is needed.

sellers.description:

deal_codes.description:

filters.description:

**Values are codes, and some are bands.** `laptop_ram_size` offers `16_gb`, not `16`, and a band includes sizes up to the next tier (`16_gb` also returns 20 GB and 24 GB machines).

Any other value is a 400 that lists the accepted values. Sorted calls return fewer restaurants than the default ranking (about 100 against up to 120), so read `total_returned` rather than assuming a sorted and an unsorted call cover the same set.

sort_direction.description:
**Which way to order the restaurants.** Optional; only meaningful with `sort`.

- `asc`  -  nearest, quickest, worst-rated or cheapest first, depending on `sort`.
- `desc`  -  furthest, slowest, best-rated or most expensive first.

It applies to `distance`, `delivery_time`, `rating_score` and `price`. Left out, `distance` and `price` come back in descending order (furthest, most expensive first) and `rating_score` best first. `sort=popularity` ignores it, and without `sort` it has no effect.

limit.description:

**120 is the most any single call returns, not just this parameter's maximum.** There is no page parameter because the directory does not paginate. Lower it for a lighter response; a larger value is a 400.
